issues.explanation: A bare `{ return $this->hasMany(Ticket::class); }` block follows the `access()` method inside the class body, which is a PHP parse error and prevents the Queue model from loading.

No migration creates the `queue_access` table, its cascading FKs or the unique `(entity_membership_id, queue_id)` index required by the task, so the model, factory, policy and actions target a table that does not exist.
The action never authorizes `$actor`, so employees, members of other entities and non-managers can create queues in any entity instead of receiving an AuthorizationException.
The action ignores `$actor` entirely, allowing any caller to rename, re-slug or deactivate any queue.
`use App\Models\UserRole;` is imported twice under the same alias, which is a PHP fatal error ('name is already in use').

`HandlesAuthorization` is imported from `Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\HandlesAuthorization`, which does not exist (the trait is `Illuminate\Auth\Access\HandlesAuthorization`), so loading the policy fatals.

`UserRole` is used as a backed enum (`UserRole::Owner->value`), but it is imported from `App\Models`; the project's role enum belongs in `App\Enums` (as `QueuePermission` demonstrates), so this is the wrong class.

The actions throw `App\Exceptions\ValidationException`/`App\Exceptions\AuthorizationException`, whereas the contract requires Laravel's `Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException` and `Illuminate\Auth\Access\AuthorizationException`, and no such app exceptions are added in the diff.

The manager check is hand-written membership SQL instead of `Gate::forUser($actor)->authorize('manageAccess', $queue)`, contradicting the task's 'policy is the single source of truth' and the project's policy/gate rule.
No Pest/PHPUnit tests ship with the change, violating the TDD convention and leaving authorization, validation, uniqueness, audit and call paths untested.
The file is replaced wholesale, deleting 156 lines covering MVP scope, roles, tickets, priorities, fairness and channels; the task asked to update the doc, not remove its content.
The ER diagram, table definitions, relationships and modeling notes are deleted and replaced with a single `queue_access` table, so the schema doc no longer describes the database.
The whole changelog (header, `[Unreleased]`, `### Added` and all prior entries) is deleted and five bullets are appended without a section heading or trailing newline.
`strlen` counts bytes, so a valid 1-255 character multibyte name can be rejected, and an all-punctuation name slugifies to an empty slug with no handling.
Every `QueryException` is reported as a duplicate slug, hiding unrelated database failures and leaving `$e` unused.
After the membership check was removed, `$entityId` is computed and never used, and `if (! Gate::forUser($user)->authorize(...)) {}` is a dead branch because `authorize()` returns void and throws.
The factory always creates a new entity, membership and queue inside `definition()`, so passing explicit IDs still leaves orphan rows and can break the same-entity invariant.
An explicit empty slug is trimmed and slugified to `''` and accepted, allowing a queue with an empty slug instead of a validation error.

Authorization uses the lazily loaded `$winner->queue` after selecting a winner rather than the already-locked, active `$queue`; a null relation would cause a TypeError at the Queue type hint instead of an AuthorizationException.
`use App\Models\QueueAccess;` and `use App\Models\User;` are redundant same-namespace imports, and the new `Gate` import is not ordered with the sibling imports.

review.summary: The change adds queue lifecycle actions, a QueueAccess model/factory, a QueuePermission enum and a QueuePolicy, but it cannot run: Queue.php has a parse error, QueuePolicy imports a non-existent trait, SetQueueAccess imports UserRole twice, and the queue_access migration is missing. CreateQueue and UpdateQueue never authorize the actor, there are no tests, and the CHANGELOG plus both requested docs are largely deleted instead of updated. Reject.
